title: How a cascade works and how adults really learn
course_title: Training-of-Trainers (ToT): Teach Adults and Build Trainers

say: How a cascade works, and how adults really learn.
This is the video for module one of the Training-of-Trainers course.
A normal training teaches a skill people use themselves. A Training-of-Trainers, or ToT, teaches two things at once: the skill, and how to teach that skill to others.

say: One small team cannot reach every village. But train 20 people properly, and if each trains 25 more, the message reaches 500 people. This chain is called a cascade.

say: The risk is dilution. Like a whispered sentence passed down a line, the message can change at each level unless you protect it.

say: For example, Amaka coordinates a women's network in Anambra. She selects 18 trainers, three in each of six local government areas, who keep their own business records and are trusted in their markets.

say: After a three-day ToT, each trainer agrees to run two sessions of about 15 women within six weeks.

say: That is 18 trainers, times 2 sessions, times 15 women: 540 women.

say: She plans honestly for drop-out. If only 15 trainers finish, the reach is 450. So her target is 450 to 540, protected by observation visits and shared forms.

say: Malcolm Knowles described how adults learn. They need to know why. They bring years of experience. They want help with real problems, and they see themselves as responsible for their own decisions.
So open with the real problem the session solves. Ask for their examples before you teach. Organise content around tasks. And give choices instead of talking down.
A market woman who has traded for 15 years already knows a great deal. Connect new tools to what she knows.
David Kolb described learning as a cycle: experience, reflect, draw the lesson, then try it. For example, Halima teaches cooperative members in Kaduna to separate business money from household money.
First, 10 minutes of experience. Two volunteers act out a trader who takes school fees from her sales box, then cannot restock.
Then 10 minutes to reflect in pairs. What went wrong? Has this happened to you?
Then 10 minutes for the concept: keep two separate purses, and pay yourself a fixed amount each week.
Finally, 15 minutes to experiment. Each woman writes her weekly amount and tells a partner who will check in.
Halima only spoke for about 10 minutes. Many trainers spend all their time explaining, and nothing changes. Use the cycle, and learning sticks.

say: Always ask before taking photos, and offer a clear option to say no. Nigeria's Data Protection Act requires personal data to be collected for a clear purpose and kept secure.

say: Run this check the evening before. Venue confirmed. Chairs in circles, not rows, and a backup if the power fails. Kit packed. Forms printed. Access and childcare planned. Co-facilitator briefed. If any box is unticked, fix it or change the plan.

To remember. A ToT teaches the content and how to teach it. Reach is trainers, times sessions, times participants. Guides, practice and follow-up stop dilution. Use all four stages of Kolb's cycle. And plan consent and inclusion before you start.
